label: EC2 Tenancy, Storage & Security — Drill 1
topic: EC2 Tenancy, User Data, Storage & Security

questions.stem: Why is there no inherent security risk when different customers' EC2 instances run on the same physical host?

options.text: Each customer is billed for the entire host regardless of usage
AWS implements advanced security mechanisms that prevent instances from accessing each other on the same host
Only one customer's instances are ever placed on a host at a time by default
Instances on a shared host cannot use the network

explanation.correct: AWS uses advanced security mechanisms that stop different customers' instances from accessing each other on the same host, so shared hosting is not a security risk.

distractors.A: Billing for the whole host describes dedicated tenancy pricing, not the isolation mechanism.
distractors.C: Default shared tenancy places multiple customers on a host; isolation—not exclusivity—provides safety.
distractors.D: Shared-host instances have full networking; connectivity is unrelated to isolation.

questions.stem: When should you choose dedicated tenancy for your EC2 workloads?

options.text: Whenever you want to minimize your overall costs
Whenever an instance needs a public IP address
When workloads must run on dedicated hardware due to internal security policies or external compliance controls
Whenever you attach more than one EBS volume

explanation.correct: Dedicated tenancy is for workloads that must run on dedicated hardware because of internal security policies or external compliance controls.

distractors.A: Default shared tenancy—not dedicated—reduces overall costs.
distractors.B: Public IP addressing is unrelated to tenancy choice.
distractors.D: Attaching EBS volumes has nothing to do with tenancy.

questions.stem: Which TWO options make up dedicated tenancy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Dedicated instances
Spot instances
Reserved instances
Dedicated hosts
Instance store volumes

explanation.correct: Dedicated tenancy comprises dedicated instances and dedicated hosts.

distractors.B: Spot instances are a purchasing option, not a dedicated-tenancy type.
distractors.C: Reserved instances are a pricing commitment, not a tenancy type.
distractors.E: Instance store volumes are ephemeral storage, not a tenancy option.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a dedicated host from a dedicated instance?

options.text: A dedicated host offers additional visibility and control over how you place instances on the physical host
A dedicated host replicates its data to another Availability Zone
A dedicated host is always cheaper than shared tenancy
A dedicated host cannot run any other resources from your account

explanation.correct: A dedicated host is effectively the same as a dedicated instance but adds visibility and control over instance placement on the physical host.

distractors.B: Cross-AZ replication describes EBS behavior, not dedicated hosts.
distractors.C: Dedicated tenancy costs more than shared tenancy, not less.
distractors.D: Dedicated hardware can be shared by other resources in your own account.

questions.stem: Which capability is specifically enabled by using dedicated hosts?

options.text: Automatic OS patching of the guest operating system
Using existing per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses tied to a specific machine
Detaching the root volume while the instance runs
Running the instance without a security group

explanation.correct: Dedicated hosts let you use existing per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses that may need to be tied to a specific machine.

distractors.A: OS patching is the customer's responsibility under the Shared Responsibility model, not a dedicated-host feature.
distractors.C: Volume detachment relates to EBS, not to dedicated-host licensing.
distractors.D: Every instance is associated with a security group regardless of tenancy.

questions.stem: Why do dedicated instances incur additional charges?

options.text: Because AWS patches their operating systems for you
Because they must always use encrypted EBS volumes
Because no other customers may run EC2 instances on the same hardware, likely leaving unused capacity
Because their data is replicated across multiple Availability Zones

explanation.correct: No other customer can run EC2 on the same hardware, so unused capacity likely remains, which is why dedicated instances cost more.

distractors.A: AWS does not patch guest operating systems; that is the customer's responsibility.
distractors.B: Encryption is optional and unrelated to dedicated-instance pricing.
distractors.D: Multi-AZ replication is an EBS/storage concept, not a pricing driver for dedicated instances.

questions.stem: When does the script entered in the EC2 User Data section run?

options.text: Every time the instance receives network traffic
During the first boot cycle of the instance
Only when the instance is terminated
Each time an EBS volume is attached

explanation.correct: User Data lets you enter commands or a script that run during the instance's first boot cycle.

distractors.A: User Data is not triggered by network traffic.
distractors.C: User Data runs at first boot, not at termination.
distractors.D: Attaching a volume does not trigger User Data.

questions.stem: On a Linux instance, what does placing `yum update -y` in User Data accomplish?

options.text: It encrypts the instance's root EBS volume
It attaches an instance store volume automatically
It creates a new security group for the instance
It updates the instance's own software automatically at boot time

explanation.correct: `yum update -y` in User Data updates the Linux instance's software automatically during boot.

distractors.A: That command updates packages; it does not encrypt volumes.
distractors.B: Instance store attachment is not performed by yum.
distractors.C: Security groups are selected during setup, not created by yum.

questions.stem: How is EC2 storage classified? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Persistent
Federated
Ephemeral (temporary)
Immutable
Replicated

explanation.correct: EC2 storage is classified as persistent or ephemeral (temporary).

distractors.B: Federated is not an EC2 storage classification.
distractors.D: Immutable is not one of the two classifications described.
distractors.E: Replication is a property of EBS, not a storage classification.

questions.stem: Which service provides persistent storage for EC2 by attaching volumes?

options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS)
Instance store volumes
Amazon Route 53
Elastic Load Balancing

explanation.correct: Persistent storage is available by attaching EBS volumes via Amazon Elastic Block Store.

distractors.B: Instance store volumes provide ephemeral, not persistent, storage.
distractors.C: Route 53 is DNS, not block storage.
distractors.D: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic and is not storage.

questions.stem: How are EBS volumes attached to an EC2 instance?

options.text: They are physically bolted to the same host as the instance
They are network-attached storage devices logically attached via the AWS network
They are embedded directly on the instance's CPU
They are mounted only through a public internet gateway

explanation.correct: EBS volumes are network-attached storage that is logically attached to the instance over the AWS network—separate devices from the instance itself.

distractors.A: Physical attachment describes instance store volumes, not EBS.
distractors.C: EBS is block storage, not part of the CPU.
distractors.D: EBS uses the AWS network internally, not a public internet gateway.

questions.stem: For resiliency, where is data on an EBS volume automatically replicated?

options.text: Across all AWS Regions globally
To the local instance store of the attached instance
Within the same Availability Zone
To an on-premises backup appliance

explanation.correct: AWS automatically replicates EBS volume data within the same Availability Zone for resiliency.

distractors.A: EBS replication is within one AZ, not across all Regions.
distractors.B: EBS does not replicate to the ephemeral instance store.
distractors.D: Replication is managed by AWS within the AZ, not to on-premises hardware.

questions.stem: What happens when you detach an EBS volume from an EC2 instance?

options.text: The data is wiped immediately for security
The data remains intact and the volume can be reattached to another instance in the same Availability Zone
The volume is converted into an instance store volume
The volume can only be reattached in a different Region

explanation.correct: Detaching an EBS volume leaves the data intact, and it can be reattached to another instance within the same Availability Zone.

distractors.A: EBS data persists through detachment; it is not wiped.
distractors.C: Detaching does not change the volume type.
distractors.D: Reattachment is within the same AZ, not necessarily a different Region.

questions.stem: Where do point-in-time snapshots of an EBS volume back up the data?

options.text: To Amazon S3
To an instance store volume
To Amazon RDS
To the instance's RAM

explanation.correct: Point-in-time EBS snapshots back up all data on the volume to Amazon S3.

distractors.B: Instance store is ephemeral and is not the snapshot target.
distractors.C: RDS is a managed database service, not the snapshot destination.
distractors.D: RAM is volatile memory, not snapshot storage.

questions.stem: Which TWO ways can you enable encryption on EBS volumes? (Select TWO.)

options.text: By enabling encryption by default for all new EBS volumes and snapshot copies from the EC2 dashboard
By rebooting the instance twice in a row
By choosing to enable encryption on a per-volume basis
By deleting the associated security group
By converting the volume to an instance store volume

explanation.correct: You can turn on encryption by default for all new EBS volumes and snapshot copies from the EC2 dashboard, or enable encryption on a per-volume basis.

distractors.B: Rebooting does not encrypt a volume.
distractors.D: Security groups are firewalls and do not control EBS encryption.
distractors.E: Converting to instance store is not an encryption method and would make storage ephemeral.

questions.stem: Which THREE events cause data on an instance store volume to be lost? (Select THREE.)

options.text: The instance is rebooted
The instance hibernates
The instance is stopped
The instance is terminated
An EBS snapshot is taken
A new security group is attached

explanation.correct: Instance store data is lost when the instance hibernates, is stopped, or is terminated (and on underlying disk failure).

distractors.A: Rebooting retains instance store data; it is not lost.
distractors.E: Taking an EBS snapshot does not affect instance store data.
distractors.F: Attaching a security group changes firewall rules, not instance store data.

questions.stem: Why are instance store volumes well suited to caching and temporary content?

options.text: Because they are automatically backed up to S3
Because they can be detached and moved between instances
Because they are physically attached to the host and therefore extremely fast
Because they are replicated across Availability Zones

explanation.correct: Instance store volumes are physically attached to the underlying host, making them extremely fast—ideal for cache and other temporary content.

distractors.A: Instance store is not automatically backed up to S3; that is EBS snapshots.
distractors.B: Instance store volumes cannot be detached from the instance.
distractors.D: Cross-AZ replication is an EBS feature, not instance store.

questions.stem: What best describes an EC2 security group?

options.text: A managed encryption key store for EBS volumes
An instance-level firewall that restricts ingress and egress traffic by source, ports, and protocols
A dedicated physical host reserved for one customer
A boot-time script that installs software

explanation.correct: A security group is an instance-level firewall that restricts inbound and outbound traffic by source, ports, and protocols; it can be associated with multiple instances.

distractors.A: Key management is not the function of a security group.
distractors.C: A reserved physical host describes dedicated tenancy, not a security group.
distractors.D: A boot-time install script is User Data, not a security group.

questions.scenario: You are provisioning a Linux and a Windows EC2 instance and must decide how the key pair is used for each.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about EC2 key pairs are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: For a Linux instance, the private key is used to remotely connect via SSH
AWS keeps the private key while you keep the public key
For a Windows instance, the private key is used to decrypt the login credentials, including the password
The public key is used to decrypt the username and password
A separate key pair must be created for every single instance

explanation.correct: On Linux the private key connects via SSH, and on Windows the private key decrypts the login credentials including the password.

distractors.B: AWS keeps the public key; the private key is your responsibility.
distractors.D: The public key encrypts the credentials; the private key decrypts them.
distractors.E: The same key pair can be used across multiple instances.

questions.scenario: Your team reuses one key pair across several EC2 instances to avoid managing many private keys, and that private key is later exposed.
questions.stem: What is the main risk of this situation?

options.text: The instances will automatically terminate
Access could be gained to any instance that uses that key pair
The EBS volumes will be wiped
AWS will rotate the public key on your behalf

explanation.correct: Because the same key pair can be reused across instances, a compromised private key could grant access to any instance that uses it.

distractors.A: A compromised key does not terminate instances.
distractors.C: Key compromise does not wipe EBS volumes.
distractors.D: AWS does not automatically rotate your key pair; safeguarding the private key is your responsibility.
